exposure: In situ uterine repair during caesarean section
cohort: Five hundred women undergoing caesarean section under spinal anaesthesia were randomized into two equal groups (uterine exteriorization vs. in situ repair).
finding: Uterine exteriorization during caesarean section offers intraoperative advantages of shorter closure time, reduced blood loss, and smaller hemoglobin decline but is associated with increased postoperative pain, with both techniques showing similar outcomes for other morbidities and hospital stay.
